arabic: وَ الْآخِرِ بِلَا آخِرٍ يَكُونُ بَعْدَهُ
الَّذِي قَصُرَتْ عَنْ رُؤْيَتِهِ أَبْصَارُ النَّاظِرِينَ ،
وَ عَجَزَتْ عَنْ نَعْتِهِ أَوْهَامُ الْوَاصِفِينَ .
لَا يَمْلِكُونَ تَأْخِيراً عَمَّا قَدَّمَهُمْ إِلَيْهِ ،
وَ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَقَدُّماً إِلَى مَا أَخَّرَهُمْ عَنْهُ.
وَ جَعَلَ لِكُلِّ رُوحٍ مِنْهُمْ قُوتاً مَعْلُوماً مَقْسُوماً مِنْ رِزْقِهِ ،
وَ لَا يَزِيدُ مَنْ نَقَصَ مِنْهُمْ زَائِدٌ .
ثُمَّ ضَرَبَ لَهُ فِي الْحَيَاةِ أَجَلًا مَوْقُوتاً ،
قَبَضَهُ إِلَى مَا نَدَبَهُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ مَوْفُورِ ثَوَابِهِ ،
لَوْ حَبَسَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ مَعْرِفَةَ حَمْدِهِ
عَلَى مَا أَبْلَاهُمْ مِنْ مِنَنِهِ الْمُتَتَابِعَةِ ،
وَ أَسْبَغَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ نِعَمِهِ الْمُتَظَاهِرَةِ ،
وَ تَوَسَّعُوا فِي رِزْقِهِ فَلَمْ يَشْكُرُوهُ .
لَخَرَجُوا مِنْ حُدُودِ الْإِنْسَانِيَّةِ إِلَى حَدِّ الْبَهِيمِيَّةِ
فَكَانُوا كَمَا وَصَفَ فِي مُحْكَمِ كِتَابِهِ :
{إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا}.
وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى مَا عَرَّفَنَا مِنْ نَفْسِهِ ،
وَ فَتَحَ لَنَا مِنْ أَبْوَابِ الْعِلْمِ بِرُبُوبِيَّتِهِ ،
وَ دَلَّنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْإِخْلَاصِ لَهُ فِي تَوْحِيدِهِ ،
وَ جَنَّبَنَا مِنَ الْإِلْحَادِ وَ الشَّكِّ فِي أَمْرِهِ .
حَمْداً نُعَمَّرُ بِهِ فِيمَنْ حَمِدَهُ مِنْ خَلْقِهِ ،
وَ نَسْبِقُ بِهِ مَنْ سَبَقَ إِلَى رِضَاهُ وَ عَفْوِهِ .
حَمْداً يُضِيءُ لَنَا بِهِ ظُلُمَاتِ الْبَرْزَخِ ،
وَ يُسَهِّلُ عَلَيْنَا بِهِ سَبِيلَ الْمَبْعَثِ ،
وَ يُشَرِّفُ بِهِ مَنَازِلَنَا عِنْدَ مَوَاقِفِ الْأَشْهَادِ ،
يَوْمَ تُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَ هُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ ،
يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئاً وَ لَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ .
حَمْداً يَرْتَفِعُ مِنَّا إِلَى أَعْلَى عِلِّيِّينَ
حَمْداً تَقَرُّ بِهِ عُيُونُنَا إِذَا بَرِقَتِ الْأَبْصَارُ ،
وَ تَبْيَضُّ بِهِ وُجُوهُنَا إِذَا اسْوَدَّتِ الْأَبْشَارُ .
حَمْداً نُعْتَقُ بِهِ مِنْ أَلِيمِ نَارِ اللَّهِ
فِي دَارِ الْمُقَامَةِ الَّتِي لَا تَزُولُ ،
وَ مَحَلِّ كَرَامَتِهِ الَّتِي لَا تَحُولُ .
وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي اخْتَارَ لَنَا مَحَاسِنَ الْخَلْقِ ،
وَ جَعَلَ لَنَا الْفَضِيلَةَ بِالْمَلَكَةِ عَلَى جَمِيعِ الْخَلْقِ ،
وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَغْلَقَ عَنَّا بَابَ الْحَاجَةِ
الَّتِي لَمْ نُفِدْهَا إِلَّا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ ،
فَلَوْ لَمْ نَعْتَدِدْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ إِلَّا بِهَا
فَمَا هَكَذَا كَانَتْ سُنَّتُهُ فِي التَّوْبَةِ لِمَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَنَا ،
لَقَدْ وَضَعَ عَنَّا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ،
وَ لَمْ يَدَعْ لِأَحَدٍ مِنَّا حُجَّةً وَ لَا عُذْراً .
وَ السَّعِيدُ مِنَّا مَنْ رَغِبَ إِلَيْهِ .
وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بِكُلِّ مَا حَمِدَهُ بِهِ أَدْنَى مَلَائِكَتِهِ إِلَيْهِ
ثُمَّ لَهُ الْحَمْدُ مَكَانَ كُلِّ نِعْمَةٍ لَهُ عَلَيْنَا
وَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ عِبَادِهِ الْمَاضِينَ وَ الْبَاقِينَ
عَدَدَ مَا أَحَاطَ بِهِ عِلْمُهُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْأَشْيَاءِ ،
حَمْداً يَكُونُ وُصْلَةً إِلَى طَاعَتِهِ وَ عَفْوِهِ ،
وَ عَوْناً عَلَى تَأْدِيَةِ حَقِّهِ وَ وَظَائِفِهِ .
حَمْداً نَسْعَدُ بِهِ فِي السُّعَدَاءِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَائِهِ ،
وَ نَصِيرُ بِهِ فِي نَظْمِ الشُّهَدَاءِ بِسُيُوفِ أَعْدَائِهِ ،
transliteration: wa lā yastaṭī‘ūna taqadduman ilā mā akhkharahum ‘anh.
Wa ja‘ala likulli rūḥin minhum qūtan ma‘lūman maqsūman min rizqih,
wa lā yazīdu man naqaṣa minhum zā’id.
Thumma ḍaraba lahu fi-l-ḥayāti ajalan mawqūtā,
Qabaḍahu ilā mā nadabahu ilayhi min mawfūri thawābih,
wa tawassa‘ū fī rizqihi falam yashkurūh.
fakānū kamā waṣafa fī muḥkami kitābih:
{In hum illā ka-l-an‘āmi bal hum aḍallu sabīlā}.
wa fataḥa lanā min abwābi-l-‘ilmi bi-rubūbiyyatih,
wa dallanā ‘alayhi mina-l-ikhlāṣi lahu fī tawḥīdih,
wa jannabanā mina-l-ilḥādi wa-sh-shakki fī amrih.
Ḥamdan nu‘ammaru bihi fīman ḥamidahu min khalqih,
wa nasbiqu bihi man sabaqa ilā riḍāhu wa ‘afwih.
yawma tujzā kullu nafsin bimā kasabat wa hum lā yuẓlamūn,
yawma lā yughnī mawlan ‘an mawlan shay’an wa lā hum yunṣarūn.
Ḥamdan nu‘taqu bihi min alīmi nāri-llāh
Allatī lam nufidhā illā min faḍlih,
Falaw lam na‘tadid min faḍlihi illā bihā
Fa mā hakadhā kānat sunnatuhu fi-t-tawbati liman kāna qablanā,
Laqad waḍa‘a ‘annā mā lā ṭāqata lanā bih,
wa lam yada‘ li-aḥadin minnā ḥujjatan wa lā ‘udhrā.
Wa-l-ḥamdu lillāhi bikulli mā ḥamidahu bihi adnā malā’ikatihi ilayh
Thumma lahu-l-ḥamdu makāna kulli ni‘matin lahu ‘alaynā
Ḥamdan yakūnu wuṣlatan ilā ṭā‘atihi wa ‘afwih,
Ḥamdan nas‘adu bihi fi-s-su‘adā’i min awliyā’ih,
wa naṣīru bihi fī naẓmi-sh-shuhadā’i bi-suyūfi a‘dā’ih,
translation: Praise belongs to God,
the First without a first before Him,
and the Last without a last after Him.
He Whom the gazes of the onlookers fall short of seeing,
and the imaginations of the describers fail to describe Him.
He originated the creation through His power, originating [them],
and He invented them according to His will, inventing [them].
Then He made them travel the path of His will,
and He dispatched them on the way of His love,
They have no power to delay that to which He has advanced them,
nor can they advance that which He has kept them back from.
And He assigned to each soul among them a known, apportioned sustenance from His provision,
No decreaser can decrease him whom He has increased,
nor can any increaser increase him whom He has decreased among them.
Then He appointed for him in life a timed term,
and set up for him a limited period,
He steps toward it with the days of his lifetime,
and approaches it with the years of his age,
until, when he reaches the end of his track,
and completes the count of his life-span,
He seizes him to that which He has called him - His abundant reward
or His dreaded punishment -
'to repay those who did evil with what they wrought
and repay those who did good with goodness.'
Out of His justice.
Holy are His names,
and manifest are His bounties.
'He shall not be questioned as to what He does,
but they shall be questioned.'
And praise belongs to God Who,
had He withheld from His servants the knowledge of praising Him
for the consecutive favours He has tested them with,
and the manifest blessings He has lavished upon them,
they would have moved about in His favours but not praised Him,
and widened [their portion] in His provision but not thanked Him.
And had they been thus,
they would have surely departed the bounds of humanity for the limit of beastliness,
and become as He has described in His firm Book:
'They are only like cattle; nay, they are even farther astray from the way!'
And praise belongs to God for what He has made known to us of Himself,
and inspired us [to offer] of thanks to Him,
and opened for us of the doors of knowledge of His Lordship,
and guided us through it to sincerity [towards Him] in professing His Unity,
and made us avoid deviation and doubt in His affair.
A praise through which we may be given long life among those of His creation who praise Him,
and through which we may race ahead of those who have raced to His good pleasure and pardon.
A praise that will illuminate for us the darknesses of the Isthmus (Barzakh),
and make easy for us the path of Resurrection,
and give us honour at the stations of the witnesses,
'on the day every soul will be repaid for what it has earned - they shall not be wronged',
'the day a master shall avail nothing a client, nor shall they be helped.'
A praise which will rise from us to the highest 'Illiyyin
'in a book inscribed, witnessed by those brought nigh.'
A praise whereby our eyes may be cooled when the sights are dazzled,
and our faces whitened when the skins are blackened.
A praise through which we may be released from the painful Fire of God
into the generous proximity of God.
A praise with which we may crowd His angels brought nigh,
and join His prophets, the envoys,
in the Abode of Permanence which does not pass away,
the place of His generosity which does not alter.
And praise belongs to God Who chose for us the beauties of creation,
and made flow upon us the delicacies of provision.
And He assigned us excellence through dominion over all creation;
thus all His creatures are submitted to us by His power,
and have come over to our obedience by His Might.
And praise belongs to God Who locked for us the door of need
except toward Him.
So how can we sustain His praise?
Or when can we render His thanks?
Nay, when?
And praise belongs to God
Who composed in us the instruments of expansion,
and appointed for us the agents of contraction,
and gave us to enjoy the spirits of life,
and fixed in us the limbs of works,
and nourished us with the delicacies of provision,
and enriched us by His bounty,
and gave us possessions through His graciousness.
Then He commanded us, to test our obedience,
and He prohibited us, to try our gratitude.
So we turned aside from the path of His command,
and rode upon the backs of His warning.
Yet He rushed us not to His punishment,
nor hastened us on to His vengeance.
Rather, He dealt slowly with us through His mercy, generously,
and awaited our return through His clemency, patiently.
And praise belongs to God
Who showed us the way to repentance,
which we would not have won save through His bounty.
For had we counted as His bounty nothing but this,
His trial upon us would indeed have been good,
His beneficence toward us great,
and His favour upon us immense.
For such was not His precedent in repentance for those who went before us.
He has surely lifted from us what we have not the strength [to bear].
He has charged us only to our capacity,
and imposed upon us only what is easy,
and left none of us with argument or excuse.
So the perisher among us is he who perishes despite Him,
and the felicitous among us is he who beseeches Him.
And praise belongs to God with all the praise with which He is praised by the nearest of His angels to Him,
the most honoured of His creatures unto Him,
and the most pleasing of His praisers before Him;
A praise that surpasses other praise
just as our Lord surpasses all His creatures.
Then to Him belongs praise, in place of every favour He has bestowed upon us
and upon all His servants, past and remaining,
to the number of all things His knowledge encompasses,
and in place of each one of those favours,
their number doubling and redoubling
always and forever,
until the Day of Resurrection.
A praise whose bound has no utmost end,
whose number has no calculation,
whose limit cannot be reached,
and whose period cannot be interrupted.
A praise which will be a link to His obedience and pardon,
a cause of His good pleasure,
a means to His forgiveness,
a path to His Garden,
a protector against His vengeance,
a security against His wrath,
a support for obeying Him,
a barrier against disobeying Him,
an aid in fulfilling His right and His duties.
A praise through which we may be happy among the happy ones of His friends,
and become joined with the martyrs slain by the swords of His enemies.
Surely He is a Friend, Praiseworthy.
